title: Council tax charges and instalments 2026/27
text: These charges apply from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 and replace the 2025/26 charges. Average annual council tax across the county, including the county, fire and police precepts but before town and parish precepts, is: Band A £1,489.24, Band B £1,737.45, Band C £1,985.66, Band D £2,233.87, Band E £2,730.29, Band F £3,226.70, Band G £3,723.12 and Band H £4,467.74. From 2026/27 bills are payable in 12 monthly instalments from April to March by default. Residents who prefer the old pattern of 10 monthly instalments from April to January can ask for it at any time before 30 April. Direct debit customers can choose a payment date of the 1st, 10th, 20th or 28th of the month; all other methods are due on the 1st. If an instalment is missed, a reminder notice gives 7 days to bring the account up to date. If a second instalment is missed in the same year, the right to pay by instalments is lost and the whole remaining balance becomes due. Court summons costs of £85 are added if the council has to apply for a liability order.

title: Council tax charges and instalments 2025/26 (superseded)
text: Superseded on 1 April 2026 by the 2026/27 charges; kept for reference for residents checking last year's bills. Average annual council tax across the county for 2025/26, including the county, fire and police precepts but before town and parish precepts, was: Band A £1,405.67, Band B £1,639.95, Band C £1,874.22, Band D £2,108.50, Band E £2,577.05, Band F £3,045.61, Band G £3,514.17 and Band H £4,217.00. In 2025/26 bills were payable in 10 monthly instalments from April to January by default, with 12 instalments available on request. Direct debit customers could choose the 1st or the 15th of the month. The reminder and summons process was the same as now, except that court summons costs were £76. Residents who moved into the county part way through 2025/26 were billed from the date they moved in, with the first instalment due 14 days after the bill was issued. Refunds of overpaid 2025/26 council tax are still made on request, by bank transfer within 10 working days.

title: Council tax discounts, exemptions and premiums
text: Single person discount: if only one adult aged 18 or over lives in a property, the bill is reduced by 25 percent. Tell us within 21 days of becoming the only adult; the discount can be backdated by up to 6 months only, even if you lived alone for longer. Students: full-time students are disregarded when counting adults, and a property occupied only by full-time students is exempt. Care leavers: young people who left the council's care are exempt from council tax until their 25th birthday, if they live in the county. Empty homes: there is no discount for empty properties, whether furnished or unfurnished, and this includes homes undergoing major repairs or renovation; the full charge applies from the day the property becomes empty. After 12 months empty, a premium of 100 percent is added, rising to 200 percent after 5 years. Second homes: from 1 April 2026 a premium of 100 percent applies to furnished homes that are no one's main residence. Annexes used by a family member as their main home get a 50 percent discount. Council tax reduction for people on low incomes is applied for separately.

title: Household bin collections and missed bins
text: Grey general waste bins and blue recycling bins are collected on alternate weeks, and the food waste caddy is collected every week. Bins must be at the kerbside by 6:30 am on collection day and taken back in the same evening. Collections go ahead as normal on bank holidays, including Easter Monday and the August bank holiday; the only days without collections are Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day, when collections move to the following Saturday. If your bin was out on time and was missed, report it online or by phone by 5 pm on the next working day. Missed general waste and food waste are collected within 2 working days of the report. Missed recycling is not returned for: put the extra recycling out in clear bags next to your blue bin on your next recycling day and it will be taken. Lids must close fully; bins with lids forced open by extra bags are not emptied. Replacement bins cost £28 including delivery, except where the crew damaged the bin.

title: Garden waste subscription 2026/27
text: Garden waste collection is an optional subscription and is not covered by council tax. For 2026/27 the price is £56 per bin for the year, collected every two weeks. Residents who signed up before 1 March 2026 paid the early sign-up price of £49. A second bin at the same address costs £44. Households receiving council tax reduction pay half price. The subscription runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, and joining part way through the year does not reduce the price. There are no garden waste collections from 14 December 2026 to 8 January 2027 while crews support Christmas collections; this break is already reflected in the price. Accepted: grass cuttings, leaves, hedge and shrub trimmings, small branches up to 10 cm thick, weeds and dead plants. Not accepted: soil, turf, rubble, food waste, plastic bags or plant pots, and animal waste. Subscriptions can be cancelled for a full refund within 14 days of sign-up; no refunds are given after that, including when moving house within the county, though the bin licence can move with you.

title: Bulky waste collection
text: The bulky waste service collects large household items that will not fit in your bins. A collection of up to 6 items for £38 can be booked online or by phone, and each additional item costs £6, up to a maximum of 12 items per collection. Fridges and freezers are collected separately at £24 each because they need specialist handling. Items must be left at the front of the property, outside and accessible, by 7 am on the collection day; crews cannot enter homes or gardens behind locked gates. Mattresses, sofas, wardrobes that have been taken apart, white goods and garden furniture are accepted. Not accepted: building rubble, car parts, tyres, gas bottles, asbestos and more than 4 bags of loose waste. Households receiving council tax reduction get one collection of up to 3 items free in each financial year. Bookings can be cancelled for a full refund with at least 2 working days' notice; later cancellations are refunded minus a £10 administration charge.

title: Saltmarsh Quay household recycling centre
text: The Saltmarsh Quay household recycling centre on Harbour Road is open to county residents. Summer hours, from 1 April to 30 September, are 8 am to 6 pm. Winter hours, from 1 October to 31 March, are 9 am to 4 pm. The Saltmarsh Quay site is closed on Wednesdays all year, and on Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day. Cars can visit without booking. Vans, pick-ups and trailers longer than 1.8 metres need a free van permit, applied for online at least 5 working days before the visit, and each household can make 12 visits per year with a van permit. DIY waste such as rubble, plasterboard and bathroom fittings is accepted for a charge of £4 per bag or item, up to 5 bags per visit. Free items include garden waste, cardboard, glass, metal, textiles, small electricals, batteries and household paint. Proof of address may be asked for at the gate, and commercial waste is never accepted.

title: Brackenholt household recycling centre
text: The Brackenholt household recycling centre on Mill Lane is open to county residents. Summer hours, from 1 April to 30 September, are 8 am to 6 pm. Winter hours, from 1 October to 31 March, are 9 am to 4 pm. The Brackenholt site is closed on Thursdays all year, and on Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day. Cars can visit without booking. Vans, pick-ups and trailers longer than 1.8 metres need a free van permit applied for online at least 5 working days before the visit, and each household can make 12 visits per year with a van permit. Brackenholt does not accept DIY waste such as rubble or plasterboard; take these to Saltmarsh Quay. It is the only site that accepts tyres, at £5 per tyre, and the only site with a reuse shop, open Friday to Sunday from 10 am to 3 pm. Free items include garden waste, cardboard, glass, metal, textiles, small electricals and batteries. Commercial waste is never accepted.

title: Residents' and visitor parking permits, from 1 January 2026
text: These prices apply from 1 January 2026 and replace the 2024 permit tariff. A first residents' parking permit costs £68 a year, and a second permit for the same household costs £120 a year. A third permit is not available in any zone. Fully electric vehicles pay half price for a first or second permit. Permits are virtual and linked to the vehicle registration, so nothing is displayed in the windscreen. Visitor parking is booked as virtual sessions through the parking account at £1.20 per day session. Each household can buy up to 60 visitor sessions per year, counted from the date the account was opened. Residents aged 75 or over get 30 free visitor sessions a year on top of that. A permit allows parking in any permit bay in your zone when a space is available; it does not reserve a space. Permit holders who move within the same zone can transfer the permit for free; moving to a different zone needs a new permit, with a refund for complete unused months.

title: Residents' and visitor parking permits, 2024 tariff (superseded)
text: This tariff is superseded by the permit prices that took effect on 1 January 2026 and is kept for reference only. Under the 2024 tariff a first residents' parking permit cost £55 a year, and a second permit for the same household cost £95 a year. A third permit was available in zones C and F only, at £150 a year. Electric vehicles paid the same price as other vehicles. Permits were paper permits displayed in the windscreen, and a lost permit cost £15 to replace. Visitor permits were sold as books of paper scratch cards, 10 cards for £10, and each household could buy up to 100 visitor cards per year. Residents aged 75 or over received 20 free visitor cards a year. Unused scratch cards bought under this tariff remain valid until 31 December 2026 and can be exchanged for virtual sessions at the customer service centre in Oldhaven.

title: Penalty charge notices: paying and challenging
text: Penalty charges for parking contraventions are £70 for higher level contraventions, such as parking on yellow lines, and £50 for lower level ones, such as overstaying in a pay and display bay. The charge is reduced by 50 percent if paid within 14 days of the date of the notice. You can make an informal challenge online within 28 days. If your informal challenge is received within the 14-day discount period and is rejected, the council will re-offer the discount for a further 21 days from the date of the rejection letter. If you do not pay or challenge within 28 days, a notice to owner is sent to the registered keeper, and the discount is no longer available. A formal representation can then be made within 28 days of the notice to owner, and if that is rejected you can appeal to the independent traffic adjudicator. Unpaid charges increase by 50 percent with a charge certificate. Blue badge holders who forgot to display the badge can have the first such penalty in any 12 months cancelled on request.

title: Libraries: membership, loans and charges
text: Library membership is free for everyone who lives, works or studies in the county. Adults and children can borrow up to 15 items at a time, and the standard loan period is 3 weeks for books, audiobooks and DVDs. Items can be renewed up to 3 times online, by phone or in person, unless another member has reserved them. Since 1 September 2025 there are no overdue fines on any items for any age, including adult loans. Items more than 6 weeks overdue are treated as lost: the replacement cost is charged to the account, and borrowing is blocked until the item is returned or paid for. If a lost item is returned within 6 months, the replacement charge is refunded. Reservations are free. Printing and photocopying cost 15p per A4 black and white page and 60p per colour page. Oldhaven Central Library is open on Sundays from 11 am to 3 pm; the other branches are closed on Sundays and Mondays.

title: Blue badge applications and renewals
text: Blue badges let disabled people park closer to where they need to go. There is no fee for a blue badge in Kestrel Bay: the council does not charge for new badges, renewals or replacements of lost or damaged badges. Apply online or with a paper form from any library. You will need proof of identity, proof that you live in the county, a recent passport-style photo, and evidence of eligibility such as an award letter for the higher rate mobility component of a disability benefit. The council aims to make a decision within 8 weeks of receiving a complete application, and applicants who need a mobility assessment are offered an appointment within 4 weeks. Badges last up to 3 years. Renewals can be submitted up to 12 weeks before the expiry date. A stolen badge can be replaced only after the theft has been reported to the police and a crime reference number has been provided.

title: Pest control service for residents
text: The council's pest control team treats rats and mice inside residents' homes free of charge, with up to 3 visits per treatment course. Rats in gardens are also treated free if there are signs of burrows. Other treatments are charged: wasps £72 per nest, bed bugs £145 for up to 3 rooms, and cockroaches £118. Fleas are treated for £95. Residents receiving council tax reduction get a 50 percent discount on charged treatments. The service does not deal with squirrels, foxes, pigeons or bees; for honeybee swarms, the council can put you in touch with a local beekeepers' volunteer list. Appointments are available Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm, and most are booked within 3 working days of the request. Payment is taken when booking, and a charged treatment cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice is refunded minus £20. Treatments for businesses and landlords with more than two properties are not offered.

title: Reporting potholes and claiming for vehicle damage
text: Potholes on council roads can be reported online with a photo and the nearest house number or lamp post number. Each report is inspected within 5 working days. Potholes rated as an emergency, deeper than 40 mm on a main road or presenting an immediate danger, are made safe within 24 hours. Other potholes that meet the repair standard are fixed within 28 days. Trunk roads and the coast road between Saltmarsh Quay and Fenwick St Mary are managed by the national highways body, not the council, so claims for those roads must go to them. To claim for damage caused by a pothole on a council road, submit the claim form within 6 months of the incident with photos of the pothole and the damage, the location, and a repair invoice or two quotes. The council is not liable where the pothole had not been reported before the incident, or where it was within the repair period when the damage happened. Decisions on claims are made within 42 days.
